seoTitle: How to Build a Daily and Weekly Planner in ClickUp (2026)
metaDescription: Set up a daily and weekly planner in ClickUp with the Weekly Planner template, built-in priorities and recurring tasks, without burning through the free plan's 60 Custom Field uses.
intro:
ClickUp can work as a personal planner without any building from scratch. The Template Center has a ready-made Weekly Planner that creates a List with a whiteboard week grid, a board and a list view. Recurring tasks then handle the daily and weekly routines so you're not retyping them every Monday.

One thing shapes how you should set it up on the free plan. Free Forever Workspaces get 60 Custom Field uses in total, and every value you set on a task counts as one. A planner that tags every task with custom priority and category dropdowns hits that ceiling within a couple of weeks. ClickUp's built-in Priority flag and Time Estimates don't count toward it, so this guide leans on those.
costNote: Everything here works on the Free Forever plan: templates, recurring tasks, the Priorities and Time Estimates ClickApps. The limit that bites is Custom Fields, capped at 60 uses per free Workspace (paid plans are unlimited). Showing future recurring tasks on a Calendar view also needs a paid plan.

steps.heading: Open the Template Center
steps.body:
In the Home or Spaces sidebar, hover over the Space or Folder where the planner should live, click the plus icon and choose Templates. Right-clicking the Space or Folder and picking Templates does the same thing. You can also type /Template anywhere that takes text and pick Browse templates.

The Template Center opens on the Featured tab. The left sidebar filters by Template Type (Space, Folder, List, Whiteboard and so on) and by Complexity, from Beginner to Advanced.

steps.heading: Find the Weekly Planner and click Quick Use
steps.body:
Type "week" into the search box. Under Personal Use you'll see the Weekly Planner next to a Weekly Calendar and a Weekly Checklist, and Marketing and Operations have their own weekly templates.

Hover over Weekly Planner and click Quick Use to create the List straight away. If you'd prefer to choose which parts come across, click the template itself and use Use Template instead. Either way ClickUp builds the List in the background and shows an Applying template notice in the corner until it's done.

image.caption: Searching "week" in the Template Center surfaces the Weekly Planner under Personal Use, alongside a Weekly Calendar and Weekly Checklist.

steps.heading: Read the Getting Started Guide before editing the whiteboard
steps.body:
The finished List (named Planner here) opens with four views across the top: Getting Started Guide, Planner Board, List and Board. Planner Board is the whiteboard: a colour-coded column for each day, a legend, and shapes that mark the current week and month.

The Getting Started Guide explains those pieces with annotated images. The first instruction is to drag the shape that circles the week and month onto the right position. Skim it once. The whiteboard's draggable labels aren't obvious from the board alone.

image.caption: The Planner List's Getting Started Guide view, showing the colour-coded weekly whiteboard and the instruction to move the week and month shape.

steps.heading: Use built-in Priority and Time Estimates, and save Custom Fields for categories
steps.body:
For priority, use the flag on each task. ClickUp's Priorities ClickApp gives four fixed levels (Urgent, High, Normal, Low) on every plan, and you can group List and Board views by it. For how long something takes, use Time Estimates, also available on every plan. A Workspace owner or admin may need to switch either ClickApp on first under App Center > All ClickApps.

Neither of those touches your Custom Field allowance. Reserve Custom Fields for what ClickUp doesn't have natively, such as a Work/Personal dropdown. On the free plan, count before you commit: 30 tasks tagged with one dropdown is already half your 60 uses. Creating a field or adding options to it costs nothing; only setting a value on a task counts.

image.caption: The new List with the Fields panel open on the right, listing suggested and available Custom Field types, while the Applying template notice finishes in the corner.

steps.heading: Make your daily and weekly routines recurring
steps.body:
Open a task, click the dates field above the description, then click Set recurring in the lower-left of the date picker. Pick a due date, then a schedule. Daily can skip weekends, which suits a morning review. Weekly repeats on the day you choose, which suits a Sunday planning session. Custom covers anything else, such as Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Next choose when it recurs (see the table below) and whether to tick Create new task. With it ticked, each occurrence becomes a separate task, so last week's completed review stays on record. Unticked, the same task resets. Click Save.

If you don't set a time, the next instance appears at 11pm in your own timezone. A task already in a Closed status won't recur, so set this up on an open task.

steps.heading: Plan the day in List, the week on the board
steps.body: For the daily pass, use List view and group by Priority so Urgent and High sit at the top. For the weekly pass, open Planner Board and drag sticky notes into the day columns, or use Board view to move task cards between statuses as the week goes. Filters in either view cut the list down to one category when it gets crowded.

troubleshooting.problem: ClickUp won't let you set a value on a Custom Field any more
troubleshooting.cause: The Free Forever Workspace has used its 60 Custom Field uses. Each value set on a task counts, and two labels on one task count as two.
troubleshooting.fix: Move priority and effort onto the built-in Priority flag and Time Estimates, clear Custom Field values you no longer need, or upgrade. Existing values stay visible either way.

troubleshooting.problem: A recurring task never came back
troubleshooting.cause: The task was in a Closed status when recurrence was set, the List sits in an archived Space or Folder, or the task has 500 or more subtasks (including closed and archived ones). ClickUp also never creates instances dated in the past.
troubleshooting.fix: Set recurrence on an open task, unarchive the location, or trim the subtasks below 500 and set the recurrence again.

troubleshooting.problem: There's no priority flag on tasks
troubleshooting.cause: The Priorities ClickApp is off for the Workspace or this Space.
troubleshooting.fix: A Workspace owner or admin can switch it on under App Center > All ClickApps, for the whole Workspace or specific Spaces.

faq.question: Is the Weekly Planner template free?
faq.answer: Yes. Templates are available on every ClickUp plan, including Free Forever. Guests can't apply List templates, though.

faq.question: Can I use ClickUp as a planner on the free plan?
faq.answer: Yes, with one limit to plan around. Free Workspaces get 60 Custom Field uses in total, so use the built-in Priority and Time Estimates for everyday tagging and keep Custom Fields for the one or two things they're needed for.

faq.question: What's the difference between Quick Use and Use Template?
faq.answer: Quick Use creates the List immediately with everything the template includes. Use Template lets you choose what to import first. If you include Custom Fields that way, Formula Fields don't come across.

faq.question: Why can't I see next week's recurring tasks on my calendar?
faq.answer: Displaying future instances of recurring tasks in Calendar view is a paid-plan feature. On the free plan only the current instance shows.
